original_question: In the same single-impurity Fermi-gas system, and assuming m/M < 13.384 so that Efimov states have not yet appeared, determine whether there exist stable non-Efimovian bound states in vacuum larger than the already known dimer, trimer, and tetramer, such as pentamers, hexamers, or still larger impurity-plus-identical-fermion clusters, for given values of the mass ratio m/M and positive scattering length a > 0.
target_in_paper: Open Problem II.3.2: "Assuming that α_c is the lower limit for the appearance of Efimov states, can there be other larger, stable, non-Efimovian few-body states (pentamers, hexamers and so on) below that limit?"
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the model—a single impurity in a polarized 3D Fermi gas—and the parameter regime (mass ratio below the Efimov threshold), and poses the question of whether larger non-Efimovian bound states exist in vacuum (e.g., pentamers, hexamers).
missing_details: Specify that the system is at zero temperature and in the vacuum limit (zero background density).
State that interactions are tuned by a wide s-wave Feshbach resonance and governed by the zero-range Hamiltonian Eq. (1).
Define α = m/M and denote the critical mass ratio α_c at which Efimov states appear.
Clarify what is meant by "stable": energetically stable against decay into any smaller impurity-fermion clusters in vacuum.
Note that deep two-body bound states are neglected under the zero-range model.
Quantify the domain of a: positive s-wave scattering length a>0 (vacuum bound states only exist for a>0).
refined_question: In a three-dimensional, zero-temperature, polarized atomic Fermi gas at zero background density—described by the zero-range wide-resonance Hamiltonian (Eq. (1)) with s-wave scattering length a>0—let α=m/M be the impurity-to-fermion mass ratio below the Efimov threshold α_c (the smallest α for which three- or four-body Efimov states appear). For which values of α<α_c and a>0 does there exist at least one stable non-Efimovian vacuum bound state comprising one impurity plus N≥5 identical fermions (e.g., pentamer, hexamer), whose energy lies below all dissociation thresholds into any combination of smaller impurity-fermion clusters?
justification: The refined question directly quotes and formalizes Open Problem II.3.2 (section II.3.2) by specifying the Hamiltonian context, model assumptions (zero temperature, wide resonance, vacuum), parameter definitions (α<α_c, a>0), and the precise stability criterion against decay into smaller clusters. It remains tightly scoped to the paper’s original open problem without broadening the scope.
